review_notes:
I reviewed all of lines 1–85. The file adds only two new definitions: `closedUpperDisk` (`{z | ‖z‖ ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ z.im}`) and `openUpperDisk` (`{z | ‖z‖ < 1 ∧ 0 < z.im}`). Everything else is a lemma about these sets: closedness, convexity, interior, closure, frontier, and the identification of `complexInside` of the boundary curve. I found no justified finding under this rubric.

I searched Mathlib for a half-disk concept (`halfDisk`, `HalfDisk`) and found nothing. Mathlib has `UpperHalfPlane`, `Metric.ball` and `Metric.closedBall`, but the half-disk is their intersection, not an existing named concept. The file already links its definition to Mathlib through `closedUpperDisk_eq`, which rewrites it as `closedBall 0 1 ∩ imCLM ⁻¹' Ici 0`, and it uses Mathlib API (`interior_closedBall`, `Convex.closure_interior_eq_closure_of_nonempty_interior`, `isBounded_ball`) instead of rebuilding it.

I also searched the OAI project for other definitions of the same sets. The only other matching definition I found is `exteriorUpperDisk` in ExteriorJoukowski.lean (`1 < ‖w‖ ∧ 0 < w.im`), which is a different set. Other files, such as DiskBoundaryRegion.lean, use `closedUpperDisk` rather than redefining it. `complexInside`, `diskDiameter` and `diskUpperArc` are imported from other files and not defined here, so they are outside this file's scope.

Remaining uncertainty: my searches matched name and text patterns, so a set defined with a different spelling elsewhere could have been missed. Even so, I found no Mathlib definition of a half-disk for these to duplicate.
